maria: Heads-up — p99 tail spiked ~400ms on the r7-2 pool right after yesterday's kernel swap. dumping flame/prof output now, any quick mitigations? @ajay
ajay: saw the alert. looks like microbatch size drift + KV eviction churn. short-term: cap max_tokens per request and force earlier truncation? reduce tail exposure.
sasha: we already have per-route truncation but it's static. can we do dynamic truncation based on queue length or worker load? e.g. if queue_len > 8 then trim to 256 tokens.
kevin: +1. also noticed kernel-selection timeout falling back to slower path — that handoff adds 50-120ms per request at tail. might be exacerbating tails when microbatches grow.
maria: profiling snippet attached (abbreviated):
```
[profile] worker=warp-12 kernel_select=timeout fallback_kernel=slow_gemm
[latency] p50=42ms p95=180ms p99=540ms
[kv] evict_rate=0.23 ttl_miss=0.08
```
ajay: propose an adaptive_microbatcher config for short term:
```
adaptive_microbatcher:
  max_batch: 12
  target_p95_ms: 160
  max_queue_len: 10
  per_request_cap_tokens: 512
  aggressive_truncate_threshold: 95
```
sasha: question — per_request_cap_tokens will harm long-context customers. can we make it route-based (low-priority routes only)? also prefer prefix-aware truncation (drop assistant history before user prompt if necessary).
kevin: we should combine approaches: 1) immediate per-worker token cap 2) bump KV cache pinning for hot prefixes 3) rollback kernel swap on affected nodes if kernel_select timeouts don't improve.
maria: rolling a canary config now to 10% of r7-2. infra-bot: deploy plan queued -> canary group r7-2-a
infra-bot: canary deployed to r7-2-a (10% traffic). monitoring p95/p99 for next 30m.
ajay: if canary looks good we can 1) propagate adaptive_microbatcher globally 2) add kernel-selection timeout metric and auto-failover to previously stable kernel.
sasha: long-term: we need a kernel-chooser that predicts tail impact using KV hit rate + batch size distribution, not just single latency. also need per-route quality budget so truncation doesn't silently degrade customer SLAs.
maria: agree. short-term plan: monitor canary 30m, keep per-worker token cap, increase kv pin TTL by 2x, and open follow-up to track kernel rollback criteria. assigning owners: @ajay (adaptive microbatcher), @kevin (kv pin + kernel rollback runbook), @sasha (quality budget & truncation policy). :thumbsup:
kevin: noted. I'll add a quick playbook snippet for rollback and a script to collect kernel_select latency histograms.
maria: thanks — keeping this thread as the runbook for the canary. will post results in 30m.
